book.title: The Colony: The Harrowing True Story of the Exiles of Molokai
book.summary: In the bestselling tradition of In the Heart of the Sea, The Colony, “an impressively researched” (Rocky Mountain News) account of the history of America’s only leper colony located on the Hawaiian island of Molokai, is “an utterly engrossing look at a heartbreaking chapter” (Booklist) in American history and a moving tale of the extraordinary people who endured it. Beginning in 1866 and continuing for over a century, more than eight thousand people suspected of having leprosy were forcibly exiled to the Hawaiian island of Molokai -- the longest and deadliest instance of medical segregation in American history. Torn from their homes and families, these men, women, and children were loaded into shipboard cattle stalls and abandoned in a lawless place where brutality held sway. Many did not have leprosy, and many who did were not contagious, yet all were ensnared in a shared nightmare.

argument.statement: The forced exile of people suspected of having leprosy created a shared nightmare because many did not have the disease or were not contagious.

book.rationale: The book primarily explores the historical context of America's leper colony in Molokai, making it a significant account within American history while also addressing issues related to public health and medical segregation.
